criteria.A: Follow Pikaday: emit .pika-single/.pika-table markup where prev/next navigate months and .pika-button days select dates, each as a working link or button.
criteria.B: Follow vanilla-calendar: emit .vc grid markup with data-vc controls and date buttons, each navigation and selection wired to a working request.
criteria.C: Ship no grid: the native input controls and the agenda list are the whole calendar; do not emit adapter-shaped markup at all.

grid.instructions: A scriptless server library must choose the DOM contract for an optional visual month grid, or decline the grid. Rank by: works with zero client script, keeps navigation and selection operable and announced, reuses pinned stylesheet rules, and minimizes markup the library must guarantee. Which option wins?

state: @canlang/ui (CanLang lane 05) emits HTML on the server and ships no client script: every control must function through links, forms, or native inputs. The pinned daisyUI 5.7.47 calendar stylesheet provides no base component; it only themes external picker widgets (verified): cally custom elements (unusable without their defining script), React Day Picker trees, Pikaday tables, and vanilla-calendar grids. Lane 05 already serves calendar needs without any grid: native date/datetime-local inputs for fields and a day-grouped section list for agendas. C7 considers adding a month grid for date picking and agenda months. Candidate contracts are the Pikaday table shape, the vanilla-calendar grid shape, or declining the grid entirely. React Day Picker markup is React-coupled (dropdowns and nav controls assume React handlers) and is not offered. The decision binds what L1 may emit and what the library must keep styled and operable.
